steps.text: When you first open PocketBudJet, a short tour shows what it can do. Tap Next to see each card, or tap Skip Tour to get started.
Read the Terms of Service, and scroll all the way to the bottom.
Then tap Disclaimer, and scroll that to the bottom too.
Tap I Accept — Continue.

Choose whether PocketBudJet locks. Leave it off to open the app like any other app, or slide it on to ask for your phone's PIN or face each time. You can change this later in Settings. Then tap Continue to Home.
A short guide points out the main areas. The tab bar at the bottom takes you to Home, Activity, Budget, Goals, and Coach. Tap Next.
Search and Coach sit at the top of every screen. Tap Next.
Tap the menu, or swipe in from the left, for Settings, your account, and Help. Tap Next.
Toolbox holds import, export, scanners, and calculators. Tap Next.
The round button adds something new, like a transaction, a budget category, or a goal. Tap I’ve got it.
You're on Home. Next, bring in a bank statement so Home fills in with your own numbers.
To change the language, tap the menu.
Tap Preferences.
Tap Language.
Pick a language from the list. Each one is shown in its own words, like Español for Spanish.
The whole app switches right away. To switch back, tap Idioma again and pick English.
Back in English.

chapters.title: Share a statement from your bank

steps.text: The fastest way to bring in a statement is to share it straight from your bank's app. Open your statements there and pick a month.
Tap Download, then Share.
Pick PocketBudJet.
PocketBudJet opens and reads every line. In a few seconds the charges are listed for you to check. Uncheck any you don't want.
Then tap the import button at the bottom.
The summary shows what came in: your income, your expenses, and what's left. Picked the wrong file? Tap Undo this import.
Tap Done.
Home now shows your own numbers.
You can also import from inside the app. Tap the menu, then Import Center.
If the statement is already saved on your phone, tap Or browse files.
Pick the statement. PDF, CSV, and OFX files all work.
Check the list, then tap the import button.
Tap Done. Bring in each new statement the same way.
Every charge gets a category. To manage them, tap Budget, scroll down, and tap Categories.
If an import leaves charges without a category, tap Sort Uncategorized to sort them all at once.
Here every charge already has one. Tap back.
To add your own category, tap the round button.
Type a name. Pick a color, and search for an icon.
Tap Add Category. It's in your list right away, ready to use on any charge.
Home shows the month at a glance: what came in, what went out, and the difference.
Below that, a short checklist helps you finish setting up: your income, a bill, a goal, and an account. The quick buttons add an expense or income, scan a receipt, or import a statement.
This chart shows where your money went. Pick a time frame, like Month.
Tap a category to see the charges inside it.
Tap back to return to Home.
Further down are your subscriptions, best prices from your receipts, your core tools, and your latest transactions.
Tap See all to open every transaction.
Tap Activity to see every transaction. The top shows what you spent, what came in, and the difference for the month.
Use the arrows to move between months.
Tap Expenses to see only money going out, or Income for money coming in. Tap All to see everything again.
To find something fast, tap the search button and type a name or an amount.
Tap a transaction to open it.
Here you see the amount, the date, and the line from your statement. Tap Edit to change the name, amount, or date.
Mark it personal or a business expense for taxes, change its category, add a note, or attach a receipt.
Rule sorts charges like this one the same way from now on. Duplicate makes a copy, and Delete removes it.
Tap back to return to the list.
To add a transaction yourself, tap the round button.
Pick Expense or Income, then type the amount.
Say what it was for.
Tap Save and you're done. For more detail, tap More Options instead.
Pick a category, then add the store. The date is today unless you change it.
Tap Save Transaction.
It's in your list right away.
Tap Budget. The top compares what you spent this month with what came in.
Below that is your spending in each category. To set a limit, tap Edit limits.
Tap Set limit under a category, type a monthly amount, and tap Save.
The bar shows how much of the limit you've used. Turn on Rollover unused budget to carry what's left into next month.
Tap back. Further down, Budget also holds your bills, categories, spending plan, savings pots, and wish list.
Tap Goals, then Start a savings goal.
Tap Add my first goal.
Name the goal. Type the target amount, and what you've already saved.
Pick a target date, then tap Calculate from target date to see what to set aside each month.
Tap Add Goal.
The card shows how far along you are, and what you need each month to get there on time.
When you put money toward it, tap Add funds, pick or type an amount, and tap Add Funds.
The progress moves right away.
Tap Budget, then Bills.
PocketBudJet spots payments that repeat in your statements. Tap the button to track one as a bill.
The name, amount, and due day are filled in for you. Choose when you want a reminder.
Tap Add Bill.
The bill shows its due day and how many days are left. When you've paid it, tap Mark Paid. To add any other bill, tap the round button.
Tap Coach, then Reports. The top card shows this month: what came in, what went out, and the difference.
Under Find the right chart, pick a question. Tap Where did my money go?
Pick a time frame. 1M is one month, and 3M is the last three.
Each category shows its share of your spending. Tap one to see its charges.
Tap back. Each question opens the chart that answers it, like how you're trending or what's coming up.
Tap Goals, then Track a debt.
No account numbers needed. Type a name you'll recognize, what you owe, the interest rate, and the minimum payment.
Tap Add Debt.
The card shows your monthly minimums, your highest rate, and when you'll be debt-free at this pace.
To add another debt, tap Manage, then the round button, and fill it in the same way.
Tap Compare Payoff Strategies.
Type how much extra you can pay each month.
Avalanche pays the highest rate first and saves the most interest. Snowball pays the smallest balance first, for quick wins.
Below, compare how long each one takes, what it costs, and the order to pay.
Your net worth is what you own minus what you owe. Tap Coach, then Reports, and open Quarterly planning.
Tap Net Worth History, then Assets.
Your debts are already counted. To add something you own, tap the round button.
Type a name and what it's worth, and pick a category.
Tap Add Asset.
Your net worth updates right away. A snapshot is saved each month, so History shows how it changes over time.
Driving for work, a medical visit, or a charity? Log the miles for taxes. Tap Coach, then Reports, and open Tax & business.
Tap Mileage Log, then Add trip.
Pick the trip type, and type the miles. The deduction is worked out as you type.
Add what the trip was for, and where you went if you like.
Tap Save trip. Your trips and the year's total deduction are kept here, ready for tax time.
Have a question about your money? Tap Coach, then Ask.
Tap a suggested question, or type your own in the box at the bottom and tap send.
The answer comes from your own numbers. Tap a card in the answer to open the full view, or ask a follow-up.
Tap the plus to start a new conversation. Your past ones are saved under the clock.
Ask something else.
Your data stays on your phone, so keep a backup. Tap the menu, then Backup & Restore.
Tap Create Full Backup.
The backup is saved on your phone. To keep a copy somewhere else, tap Share to PC / email and pick your email, cloud storage, or computer. Here, tap Done.
On a new phone, install PocketBudJet, come back here, and tap Restore from Backup.
To have PocketBudJet ask for your phone's lock each time it opens, tap the menu, then Preferences.
Scroll down to Require app unlock, and turn it on.
Confirm with your phone's PIN, fingerprint, or face.
It's on. Close PocketBudJet and open it again.
It asks for your phone's lock first. Unlock it, and you're in.
To stop, turn Require app unlock off in Preferences.
